messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated gateway timeouts (504) and streaming disconnects detected in eu-north1. 3m error rate 6.8% (threshold 1.5%). Paging @Priya K. and @oncall-eu.

Priya K.: ack. I'm grabbing dashboards. Which flows? streaming or regular generation?

Tom B.: streaming endpoints (chat/stream) show spikes in connection resets + 504s. Non-stream (sync) has smaller bump ~1.2%.

Elena M.: looking at NAT & conntrack: several egress nodes hitting conntrack table highwater ~95%. kernel logs show "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet" on gw-eun1-*.

Maya D.: that'd explain resets. heavy fanout from our streaming keep-alives + clients re-trying. If conntrack drops packets, upstream TCP resets -> 504s.

Priya K.: quick mitigation ideas: 1) increase conntrack max on affected nodes 2) add short-term L4 bypass steer for streaming traffic to us-west2 3) enable passive short-circuit on busy routes. Thoughts?

Tom B.: agree. I'll bump net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max via sysctl on the 6 impacted gateways, but that's a temporary cushion. Need to reduce open connections too — start draining long-lived connections and steer new streams.

SRE-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2026-046. Severity: P1. Runbook assigned to @Priya K., @Tom B., @Elena M..

Elena M.: sysctl commands ready: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` and persist in /etc/sysctl.d/99-cntrack.conf. applying to gw-eun1-{03..08}. Doing rolling apply now.

Tom B.: applying traffic steer for streaming only: `rbctl traffic steer --from-region eu-north1 --to-region us-west2 --percent 60 --selector "route in (chat-stream, stream-session)"` Starting now.

Priya K.: enabling passive short-circuit for the heavy route set (if backend latency > 900ms, return 429 to clients with Retry-After) to prevent retries hammering conntrack.

Maya D.: note: returning 429 will require client-side retry logic; we'll call it out in comms. Also add a feature-flag so we can revert quickly.

support-lead: drafting status page blurb: "We are experiencing elevated timeouts affecting streaming connections in EU-North. We have temporarily routed streaming traffic to an alternate region and are applying kernel tuning. Some customers on long-lived streams may see disconnects or 429s. More updates in 15m." any additions?

Tom B.: after steer started: connection rates to eu-north borderline but stable. conntrack dropped events dropped ~70% after sysctl change. However a subset of gateways still show high tcp_inflight (long-lived). I'm initiating `kubectl drain` for gw-eun1-05 and gw-eun1-07 (no-new-conns then graceful shutdown) to clear stale flows.

Elena M.: also flushing conntrack entries for streaming tuples after drain: `conntrack -F -p tcp --dport 443 --orig-port 0-65535 --timeout 300` (dry-run then apply). Doing that now on drained nodes only.

Priya K.: telemetry 5m in: eu-north 504 rate down from 6.8% -> 2.1%. us-west2 saw ~30% increase in streaming load but no SLA breaches. Good.

Maya D.: watch for increased latency to us-west2 for EU users; the steer will raise RTT. We'll keep it only for non-prem tenants.

support-lead: support flagged 14 tenants with high streaming usage; prioritizing outreach now. sending targeted message template to support reps.

John H.: I see a pattern of ephemeral worker processes in backend-eun1-runner exiting with "EMFILE" (too many open files). Looks like file descriptor limits on some workers also contributed to instability under conntracking pressure. Need a follow-up fix but not for immediate mitigation.

Priya K.: for immediate cleanup: 1) sysctl bump done 2) conntrack flush on drained nodes done 3) traffic steer to us-west2 at 60% for streams (non-prem). 4) drain two gateways. Continue monitoring 20m then step-steer down 10% increments.

SRE-bot: Rolling restart of gateway deployment gw-eun1 (graceful) initiated (deploy-4201). ETA ~6m.

Tom B.: rolling restart done. gw-eun1 pods restarted with updated sysctl via init hook. No crash loops. conntrack evictions reduced to negligible.

Elena M.: metrics: packet drops from conntrack down to ~1/min from 120/min. streaming 504s down to 0.9%. latency p95 elevated for eu customers using us-west steer by ~60ms.

Priya K.: I propose to reduce steer to 30% for streaming now and keep non-prem steer only. If stable 15m later, move to 0% and rely on kernel tuning + descriptor limit fixes.

Maya D.: +1. Also will open an infra ticket to auto-detect conntrack spike patterns and escalate before losses accumulate.

support-lead: initial outbound messages sent to 14 tenants, internal list added for any enterprise SLA flags. No confirmed SLA violations for premium customers yet.

John H.: created issue for worker ulimit / file descriptor fix and native resource leak investigation. assigning to runtime team.

Priya K.: lowering page to P2 for observation phase. Keep channel open until final rollback of steers and postmortem. ops-bot, update INC-2026-046 -> mitigated -> monitoring.

SRE-bot: INC-2026-046 status updated to MITIGATED (monitoring). Postmortem required within 72h.

Maya D.: postmortem checklist: timeline, conntrack graphs, kernel logs, drain timings, affected tenant list, infra remediation (sysctl default increase?), app fd limits, and automatic steer runbook. Assigning to @Maya D.

Priya K.: thanks everyone. summary will go to #incidents and I'll schedule RC meeting tomorrow. re-open if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:

Tom B.: thanks team. good catch on conntrack signals.

support-lead: closing loop with support; will post final customer note after RC meeting.
